linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
Nvidia added nearly $1 trillion in market value this week following the reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. His return comes after significant pressure from President Trump, who cited the U.S. attorney general in defending the move. While the company faces ongoing export-control investigations, the market responded positively to the leadership change, helping lift the Nasdaq by 6.5 percent.

Elsewhere in the AI sector, Anthropic made history as the first pure-play AI developer to go public. The company saw a record-setting IPO, with shares opening 34 percent higher and briefly valuing the firm at over $2 trillion. Despite the strong debut, broader Wall Street indexes closed lower, and the event was met with protests outside the Nasdaq that resulted in three arrests.

In infrastructure news, the U.S. government approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a constellation of one million data satellites. Known as Starmind, the project aims to address the rising global demand for AI computing power by creating a more energy-efficient network in space.

instagram.title: Slain Gaza Journalist Wins Top International Award

slides.headline: Slain Gaza Journalist Wins Top International Award
slides.subtitle: Mariam Dagga was 33 when she was killed.

slides.explanation: The Rory Peck prize is one of the most respected honors for freelance video journalists working in dangerous conditions globally.

slides.headline: She shares the award with colleagues
slides.explanation: Dagga did not win alone. She shares this recognition with two of her fellow AP colleagues for their collective coverage of the war's human toll.
Both The Guardian and France 24 reported on the award, confirming the details independently to ensure accuracy.

slides.subtitle: Read the full story at Headlinne.com.

instagram.caption:
Mariam Dagga was a war correspondent working in Gaza when she was killed in an Israeli strike.

She was 33 years old at the time.

Organizers of the Rory Peck prize, which recognizes the work of freelance video journalists, have now awarded her the honor posthumously. She shares this recognition with two colleagues from the Associated Press.

The award highlights their coverage of the human impact of the conflict. It serves as a reminder of the immense risks journalists face while documenting war.

story.title: Palestinian journalist killed by Israel in Gaza wins Rory Peck prize
story.summary: Mariam Dagga shares award with two of her colleagues from AP for ‘powerful coverage’ of human cost of war Mariam Dagga, the Palestinian war correspondent who was killed at the age of 33 in Gaza in an Israeli strike, has posthumously won the prestigious Rory Peck prize for freelance video journalists, the organisers announced on Wednesday. She shares the award with two of her colleagues from the Associated Press (AP), Abdel Kareem Hana and Jehad Alshrafi, “for their powerful coverage of the human cost of the war” in the Palestinian territory, the Rory Peck Trust said. story_card.headline: SpaceX gets FCC approval for orbital AI data centers
story_card.standfirst: The regulator cleared a path for space-based computing despite significant pushback.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: The FCC approved a SpaceX plan to host AI data centers in orbit around Earth.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Opponents raised alarms about risks to scientific research, but the FCC dismissed them.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: The agency ruled that those specific concerns fall outside its regulatory authority.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Look for how SpaceX implements this technology and if regulatory pushback continues.

story_card.caption:
The FCC has officially approved a SpaceX plan to put AI data centers into space.

This decision comes despite fears that orbital servers could interfere with scientific research. The FCC concluded that those specific issues are not within its power to regulate. It is a major step forward for the future of space-based computing.
